Maya: heads-up — onboarding halcyon-50k (int4) revealed a deterministic token drift on very long prefill (>48k). float32 baseline matches expected. suspect RoPE wrap/phase normalization interacting with async prefetch and quant kernel tiling. :thinking_face:
Dmitri: can you paste the exact repro command and which quant artifact hash?
Maya: branch release/serve-v4, quant artifact q-int4-2024-11-07 (sha abc123). repro:
```bash
./eval/longprefill_runner --model halcyon-50k --quant int4 --context 52000 --prefetch-window 12288 --seed 20241107 --force-kernel=vector --rotary-preserve=false
```
Maya: behavior: fingerprints align until token ~49120 then diverge; logs show rope-phase wrap event then a prefetch entry applied with a mismatched request-id. snippet:
```
[11:21:10] rope: wrap at idx=49120 phase=0x7f3a scale=1.00015
[11:21:11] prefetch push shard=4 id=0x5b11 req=0x9aa1
[11:21:11] handshake ack shard=4 id=0x5b11 req=0x9aa1
[11:21:12] token-check expected=token_49121 actual=token_49120
```
Zoe: interesting — similar to other reports but different model. Two quick experiments: 1) toggle `--rotary-preserve=true` 2) force scalar kernel to see if scheduling normalizes.
Maya: ran both: scalar kernel + rotary_preserve=true -> matches float baseline. vector + preserve=false -> drifts reproducibly.
Cal: that suggests a timing/order issue where vector kernel chunking + non-preserved rotary causes keys to be encoded with relative positions that shift when windows wrap. Could be prefetch id reuse or stale kv entries being applied.
Dmitri: let's add extra invariants: attach absolute_pos and request_uuid to every kv entry and validate on lookup; also add a handshake guard that verifies sender-provided fingerprint and absolute_pos before applying. If mismatch, fail fast and log full buf.
Maya: plan: run a small matrix tonight across PREFETCH_WINDOW={8192,12288,16384}, ROTARY_PRESERVE={true,false}, KERNEL={scalar,vector}, and KERNEL_CHUNK={default,force-small}. will dump kv fingerprints + rope-phase trace. uploading results to s3://redwood-eval/halcyon_longprefill/1869991234.tar.gz
ml-bot: longprefill job queued (lp-99077). float baseline completed: pass. int4-vector reproduce: 3/3. int4-scalar matches float: 3/3.
Zoe: if scalar matches, it's likely scheduling/ordering. Dmitri, can you bisect the vector kernel commits between the scalar-matching and vector-drifting implementations?
Dmitri: will start bisect Monday. Also adding a short-lived canary with handshake guard to dedicated pool if matrix reproduces reliably. @ops-bot can we reserve 4xA100 for 2 hours at 01:00 UTC next Tue?
ops-bot: request received. reserving 4xA100 for team-ml on 2024-11-12T01:00Z-2024-11-12T03:00Z. ticket OP-7920 created.
Maya: uploading artifacts now (kv dumps, rope traces, command lines) and filing INF-1600 with TL;DR and checklist.
Cal: additional test: run with `--prefetch-sync=1` to disable async prefetch. if that avoids drift, strong evidence for race.
Maya: tried that — `PREFETCH_SYNC=1` reduces but does not fully eliminate mismatches (1/5 runs still diverged).
Zoe: okay next steps: 1) full matrix + kv/phase dumps 2) kernel bisect by Dmitri 3) handshake guard PR as hotfix if bisect proves kernel change is risky 4) canary rollout and monitor eval-harness score deltas.
Maya: checklist on INF-1600: [ ] matrix runs uploaded [ ] kv+rope traces available [ ] bisect results in ticket [ ] handshake guard PR if needed [ ] canary run scheduled
Maya: uploading now: s3://redwood-eval/halcyon_longprefill/1869991234.tar.gz (contains seeds, commands, kv-dumps). will update with matrix summary. :rocket:
